notes: One entry per concept, each its own call to GET /v1/tenders/search. MapleProcure search is SQLite FTS5: every keyword in a call must appear in the notice, so the design doc's keyword list sent as one query matches nothing. More words in a concept only narrow it.

The tokenizer is `porter unicode61`: words are stemmed (`license` and `licensing` match the same notices) and case-folded (`IT` is the pronoun `it`), and there are no synonyms or spelling variants (`licence` is not `license`).

Every concept was measured against the live service; `matches_when_measured` is total_matches at that moment. Search returns at most 100 rows and has no offset, so a concept near 100 would lose rows with no way to page. The largest here is 53. merge-results.js reports any search that comes back truncated.

Design-doc areas are listed in `covers`. Payments, grants management, budgeting and procurement technology have no concept of their own: searched alone they match payment terms, funding clauses and the word `procurement` in unrelated notices (see `excluded`). They are reached through the software, platform and financial-system concepts they intersect with.

Retrieval is favoured over precision. A notice this profile never retrieves never reaches the classifier and no metric can show it; a notice retrieved in error costs one classification and is dismissed. Concepts are kept anyway only where their hits include real software and IT procurement.

`closing_before` is deliberately not sent. It is `closing_date <= ?` in MapleProcure's SQL and would drop every notice with no closing date, invisibly. Closed notices are filtered in merge-results.js, where the exclusion is listed.

excluded.why: Case-folded to the pronoun `it`; matches a quarter of all notices and exceeds the 100-row cap.
Payment-terms boilerplate. The top hit is a solar microgrid installation. `payment processing` (23) and `electronic payment` (17) are construction notices.
Funding clauses in advance procurement notices for construction. `grant management` (13) is the same set.
Construction and housing notices only. `budgeting software` (1) is already inside `software`.
`procurement` appears in nearly every notice. Over the cap. `e-procurement` (141) tokenizes to `e` and `procurement`.
The source does not use the acronym. `enterprise resource planning` matches 1 notice, already inside `information-technology`.
Effectively `software service`: a subset of `software`. `SaaS` covers the acronym separately.
A subset of `digital`, as are `digital platform` (5) and `digital services` (24).
Over the cap; dominated by property and facilities management.
A professional-services vehicle whose streams are mostly business and project consulting. Its IT streams also match `information technology`.
